  La Verne City Hall - Council Chambers,

  In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
  modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s
  Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting. Regular Meetings are held on the 1st
  and 3rd Monday of every month.

  The Council Chambers will be opened to the public at 6:00 p.m. To facilitate public participation for
  those who do not wish to attend in person, the meeting will still be made available virtually to
  residents. Below are the following opportunities on how to participate:

  1)  View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org and click on the green “Council
  Meeting Live Stream” button.

  2)  Individuals can email their comments to the Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org up
  to noon on the day of the meeting. Those comments will be shared with City Council in advance
  of the City Council meeting and included as part of the permanent record. Please be advised
  that public comments submitted by emails or any other format to the City are public
  records that will be made available for public viewing.

  3)  Individuals who wish to share their comments directly during the meeting may do so by emailing the
  Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org with their phone number and the item(s) they wish
  to speak on. Requests will be accepted before and throughout the meeting and staff will call you
  back at the appropriate time. Once items are considered by the City Council, no further public
  comment on that matter will be accepted. A time limit of 3-minutes is set for all public comments.

  4)  If you wish to participate via Zoom, you will need to register at
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_HsvW7kMfQUKnAk3Y2BRB_A
  before 12:00 p.m. on Monday, August 01, 2022, and please be aware that space is limited. You will
  have the ability to watch the meeting in real time and raise your hand to request to comment as
  appropriate on the current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be brought into the
  meeting and have the ability to turn your video on when called upon.

 La Verne Wilderness Area
  Management Plan

City Council Study Session
  August 1, 2022
 Introduction
  The development of the Wilderness Area Management Plan
  began in 2007 and had been delayed in 2008, to 2015, due to
  the lack of funding to complete an Environmental Impact
  Report (EIR).

  In 2015, the City began the process for the EIR and
  development of the plan. The Planning Commission reviewed
  the plan and EIR in April of 2019. Due to other community
  issues that came about at this time, large development
  projects initiated by outside applicants, and then the COVID-
  19 pandemic, the project was again stalled and never made it
  to the City Council meeting for the final adoption.

  There are also new City Council members that may not be
  aware of the proposed plan and the work that has been
  completed over the years, therefore staff felt that it was
  necessary to conduct a study session to present the project in
  its entirety before going straight to a public hearing to adopt.
 Overview
  2006: the City acquired 208 acres in north La Verne through
  State grant funds obtained in cooperation with the County of
  Los Angeles, the Trust for Public Land, and the La Verne Land
  Conservancy.

  This land was combined with 150 acres already owned by the
  City to create an open space preserve of 358 acres,
  collectively referred to as the Wilderness Area.

  The Wilderness Area Management Plan includes selective
  habitat enhancement actions, the resolution of public safety
  hazards, and opportunities for limited controlled public
  access as part of the City’s stewardship responsibilities for
  the Wilderness Area.
  Time Line
 2007/2008: The City began the planning
  process for a Plan for the Wilderness Area.

 October 2008: A Draft Management Plan
  outlined recommendations for habitat
  resource enhancement, public safety actions,
  and controlled public access along with
  selected management alternatives.

 Due to a lack of funds to complete an EIR, the
  City elected to postpone any action.
 Time Line Cont.
 2015: At a City Council Workshop, staff
  presented an overview of the management
  plan findings, the cost of improvements, and
  recommended next steps.

 The City Council asked staff to prepare a
  Request for Proposal for the Project outlining
  an update of the Management Plan and the
  EIR.
 Time Line Cont.
 2016: The City re-initiated review of the
  management options to prepare an EIR.

 October 2018-2019: The Planning Commission
  conducted several meetings and additional
  information was requested. Feedback was
  received from residents and other state
  agencies.

 January 9, 2019: Returned to the Planning
  Commission meeting, where staff provided an
  update related to the meaning of “public
  access” and the revised resolution proposing a
  two phased plan.
 Planning Commission Recommendation

  The Planning Commission recommended 2 phases.

  Phase 1 consists of maintenance, security, fuel modification,
  planting, and protecting the wilderness area.

  Phase 2 includes the development of the loop trail and the
  increase of public access to the area. Conditions were also
  added that if there is ever a desire for Phase 2 to move forward,
  an update to the EIR (as necessary), a public workshop, and City
  Council approval would be required prior to implementation, to
  ensure that Phase 2 will only move forward with proper
  notification to the residents and ultimately a vote of the City
  Council.

  April 10, 2019: The Planning Commission voted to recommend
  approval to the City Council.
 Next Steps
 Public notice will be mailed out
 to the adjacent community in
 mid August
